title: How disputed rune readings change the measurements
question: If the 450 located O/A/AE machine disagreements were read differently, which manuscript statistics move, and how does one known-key decoder respond to separately simulated transcription errors?
reader_question: How much could disputed rune readings change what we measure?
summary: Hypothetically replacing all 450 source-suggested O/A/AE alternatives raises joined-stream adjacent repeats from 86 (0.664%) to 103 (0.795%), below the source comparison floor of 126, but shifts normalized IoC from 0.999874 to 1.013823. Known-key LP1 decoder fixtures degrade with separate random ciphertext errors. The reader controls reuse global canonical labels and do not establish independent transcription accuracy. A separately recovered exact KJV input also permits the source's six-level full-book decoder replay; its results are fixture-specific.
finding: A fresh source replay maps all 450 alternatives and reproduces the full 400-trial perturbation grids. Exact all-450 changes add 17 joined-stream adjacent repeats (86/12955 pairs, 0.664%; to 103/12955, 0.795%) and shift normalized IoC 0.999874→1.013823. In separate planted LP1 key-skip fixtures, median recovery first falls below 90% at book-equivalent k=1800 (L120) and k=900 (L400). In the separate 12,956-rune KJV fixture (six replicates per level), median recovery first falls below 90% at k=450, when correct/wrong-key scores still separate; score distributions overlap at k=900. Fresh nested results match the archived source apart from elapsed seconds.
limitations: The 450 source-reader disagreements are not adjudicated image errors. Source T1 controls are transductive because global canon-derived labels include the test pages. The decoder corrupts synthetic LP1 ciphertext uniformly, not the 450 LP2 locations, and tests one key-skip model with English scoring. The exact full-book KJV fixture was replayed, but uses a different plaintext register as well as length and has six replicates per level. The source dependency graph was not freshly rebuilt. No broad LP2 cipher exclusion follows.
next_steps: Rebuild glyph labels with solved controls strictly held out before estimating transcription error; then test predeclared image-adjudicated alternatives and decoder controls that match the proposed cipher and error locations.

sources.label: Pinned source T3 preregistration and programs

reader_finding: Changing all 450 proposed rune readings adds 17 adjacent repeats and shifts the frequency statistic. These are hypothetical alternatives, not 450 confirmed errors. In a separate full-length known-key fixture, 450 random changes reduce median recovery to 86%.
reader_limit: The reader was trained using canonical labels from the control pages too, so its agreement does not independently establish accuracy. The decoder controls cover one model and simulated errors. The short and full-length fixtures also use different plaintext texts.
